# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized

  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record

# gh-1425: [GOAL] Resume loses structured-compaction folds — marathon session reopens at 143% of window; make fold projection resume-equivalent and cap every detonation path

## Description

## Goal — Compaction/checkpoint composition (v2)
One sentence: **a marathon session resumed after close/reopen restores the same visible context it had before the close — structured-compaction folds survive the resume byte-faithfully, and no single event (boot or user turn) can leave the live context above the model's window.**

Live RCA from a real 36-day session (`01a06644-7b1b-72b2-b9ea-2e1971a36251`, CLI updated 1.0.531→1.0.532 between close and reopen, 2026-10-08):

## RCA (measured on the session file, mechanisms pinned to code)
- Session JSONL: **2.01 GB, 19,112 records.** Kinds: 9,862 message, 9,131 custom, **6 classic `compaction` (last at index 3,081)**, 5 `branch_summary`, **24 `hidden_range`** (last at 19,040; 77 records / 1.74 MB after), **14 `compact_checkpoint`** (9,185→19,037).
- **Compaction DID run the whole time — as STRUCTURED compaction.** The classic LLM-summary `compaction` record stopped at 3,081; from there the structured engine owned the context: `hidden_range` + `compact_checkpoint` records ARE its folds (`engine.dart:260/413/540 appendHiddenRange(recordIds:…)`, `engine.dart:603 appendCompactCheckpoint`). v1 of this card wrongly claimed "no compaction for 5 weeks" — retracted: the owner watched compactions happen live; only the RECORD KIND differs.
- **The resume did not reproduce the pre-close fold projection.** Before close the visible context was ≈100k tokens (the fold markers in the transcript cover e.g. `0-439:ckpt·98k→3.4ktok`). After reopen the ctx meter showed **143% of 200k (≈286k) at idle boot, before any user message** — roughly the pre-close visible set PLUS a large fraction of folded debt back in view. The fold chain half-applied.

Primary suspects (need one repro to separate):
1. **RecordId anchor skew:** folds persist `recordIds`; a resume that rebuilds record identities differently across the CLI version boundary (or across branch/merge points) orphans the ranges → dropped.
2. **Depth-cap flattening divergence:** `engine.dart:767 _flattenForDepthCap` flattens nested `CompactCheckpointRecord`s — if boot's flatten pass differs from the live one (order/depth bookkeeping), the visible set grows.
3. **Version skew 1.0.531→1.0.532:** a record shape or ledger rule change between the binary that wrote the folds and the binary that replays them, silently skipping older folds.

Secondary legs (still true, now clearly subordinate):
- **S1 — no boot cap:** nothing force-compacts an over-window session at resume; the `force` path exists (`auto_compactor.dart:223/275`) but boot never uses it. The meter faithfully displayed 143% and waited.
- **S2 — gate blindness (consequence, not cause):** `auto_compactor.dart:263 _requestTokens()` gates on the post-fold visible list only. That is by design for structured compaction (folds are cheap, expansion on demand), but it is why the file grew to 2.01 GB of recoverable debt with no classic compaction record — the debt is invisible to every budget surface until a fold-loss event detonates it.
- **S3 — userTurn detonation:** a real user turn auto-closes checkpoints (`checkpoint_tool.dart:235 _stalenessReason`, #286 — correct) restoring hidden spans at once; without a budget guard this is a second path to the same balloon.

## Why this framing
Retracted (v1): "resume miscounts tokens" — the meter is honest. Retracted (v1→v2): "no compaction ran for 16k records" — structured compaction ran constantly; only classic records stopped. Kept: the detonation framing — several independent events (fold-loss resume, userTurn auto-close) can each push the live context far past the window, and nothing reconciles folded debt against any budget.

## Architecture
- **Fold-projection equivalence (primary fix):** the ledger replay at resume MUST reproduce the live engine's visible set — same fold application, same depth-cap flatten, same recordId resolution; verified by an equivalence property test (replay-vs-live byte-comparison of the projected payload on forked fixtures), not by spot checks.
- **Version-skew tolerance:** fold records carry enough shape metadata that a newer binary replays older folds or FAILS LOUD (a resume note naming the dropped fold generation), never silently half-applies.
- **Boot cap:** resume of an over-window session runs one forced compaction pass before the first request (S1); the meter renders the post-cap number.
- **Budget-guarded restore (S3):** checkpoint auto-close restores hidden spans only up to a budget; the remainder routes into a forced pass. Degradation: compactor failure → local trim (existing), never a silent over-window request.
- **ComposedBudgetEstimator (S2, second tier):** one pure function (visible + hidden debt) for the gate/meter/boot so debt is visible before it detonates.

## Capability surface (subject of every verb)
| capability | acts on | shape |
|---|---|---|
| replay | the **persisted fold chain** (`hidden_range`+`compact_checkpoint` records) | equivalence with the live projection, byte-verified |
| tolerate | **older fold record shapes** across CLI versions | loud-fail note listing dropped generations |
| cap | the **resumed context** at boot | one forced pass; meter shows post-cap |
| restore | **hidden spans** at checkpoint auto-close | budget-capped, remainder compacted |
| surface | the **composed budget** (visible+debt) | same number in gate/meter/boot (second tier) |

The budget-stop branch returns `true` (not false) after trimming: `_trimTokenBudget(branch, tokenBudget); return true;`. - Boundary found but kept path not resident → walk continues (instead of returning true).

What if the newest compaction record's `firstKeptEntryId` points to a record that is NOT on the active branch (corrupted/off-branch)? Then `branch.any(...)` never true → walk pages to file head (all residency) → return true at `_hasOlder == false`. Bounded by maxPages * block size. - **Title**: gh-1425 [GOAL] Resume loses structured-compaction folds — marathon session reopens at 143% of window make fold projection resume-equivalent and cap every detonation path
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1425` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 13
- **Additions**: +1612
- **Deletions**: -45
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T20:46:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T22:44:12Z

## PR Description

Closes #1425
# gh-1425 — Resume loses structured-compaction folds (marathon session)

### Root Cause
Resuming a marathon session did not reproduce the live fold projection — three legs:
- `WindowedSessionStorage.growOlderUntil` stopped the resume boundary walk when the branch *contained* the newest classic compaction record, but the kept region starts at `firstKeptEntryId` — a walk block-bottom landing inside the kept span silently dropped the whole kept region (residency skew), so folds half-applied over a different record population.
- `renderStructuredMessages` applied every fold record as-is, with no resolution check: a fold the replaying binary cannot resolve (an older writer stored the ids under keys this build does not read — empty id shape) still rendered its checkpoint text as a valid summary over nothing.
- Resume boot never capped an over-window session (the meter sat at 143% and waited); and the degraded local-trim valve kept `keepRecentTokens` *transcript* tokens while the trigger measures *request* tokens (incl. system-prompt/tool overhead), so a degraded boot landed back over the trigger and re-fired compaction on turn 1.

### Fix
- `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`: `growOlderUntil` now keeps paging until the classic boundary's `firstKeptEntryId` is resident (`ensureCompactionBoundaryResident`) — the resumed replay sees the full kept path.
- `lib/src/compaction/structured/projection.dart`: all-or-note fold resolution — a fold the replaying binary cannot resolve (empty id shape: an older writer's keys this build does not read) is dropped WHOLE, never applied, and a visible resume note names it (seq + kind). Off-path references (off-branch checkpoint coverage, below-window ranges) are not skew and render exactly as before (REG-1).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart` + `session_commands.dart`: resume boot cap — `_loadSession` runs one gated forced compaction pass at idle boot (also on mid-REPL session switches) so the meter renders the post-cap number before the first user message.
- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: `_localTrimFallback` clamps its kept budget to `min(keepRecentTokens, trigger − overhead)` so a degraded (summarizer-down) boot stays under the compaction trigger and the session remains usable without a working summarizer.

### Test Coverage
- `test/session/windowed_session_storage_test.dart` — boundary walk keeps paging until `firstKeptEntryId` is resident (RED before fix).
- `test/compaction/structured_resume_equivalence_test.dart` — live-vs-resume projection byte-shape equality over a marathon fixture with a forked branch and folded checkpoints; AC2 tests: empty-shape hidden range and checkpoint dropped whole with a note, off-path refs apply unchanged with no note.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_resume_boot_cap_test.dart` — AC3: cap pass runs before any user input and the next request fits the window; AC5: dead summarizer degrades to the visible `[context trimmed]` note, boot survives, turn 1 answers without re-firing compaction.
- Full suite: `dart test test/compaction test/agent test/cli` green (see notes on the earlier native abort).

### Notes
- Healthy fold rendering is intentionally unchanged (REG-1 asserted byte-shape equality) — only unresolvable folds change behavior, and only by becoming visible notes instead of silent half-applies.
- The resume note is one user-role message; it adds no hidden context and keeps the `window − reserve` invariant via the existing pre-flight gate.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, us…

# gh-1425: [GOAL] Resume loses structured-compaction folds — marathon session reopens at 143% of window; make fold projection resume-equivalent and cap every detonation path

## Description

## Goal — Compaction/checkpoint composition (v2)
One sentence: **a marathon session resumed after close/reopen restores the same visible context it had before the close — structured-compaction folds survive the resume byte-faithfully, and no single event (boot or user turn) can leave the live context above the model's window.**

Live RCA from a real 36-day session (`01a06644-7b1b-72b2-b9ea-2e1971a36251`, CLI updated 1.0.531→1.0.532 between close and reopen, 2026-10-08):

## RCA (measured on the session file, mechanisms pinned to code)
- Session JSONL: **2.01 GB, 19,112 records.** Kinds: 9,862 message, 9,131 custom, **6 classic `compaction` (last at index 3,081)**, 5 `branch_summary`, **24 `hidden_range`** (last at 19,040; 77 records / 1.74 MB after), **14 `compact_checkpoint`** (9,185→19,037).
- **Compaction DID run the whole time — as STRUCTURED compaction.** The classic LLM-summary `compaction` record stopped at 3,081; from there the structured engine owned the context: `hidden_range` + `compact_checkpoint` records ARE its folds (`engine.dart:260/413/540 appendHiddenRange(recordIds:…)`, `engine.dart:603 appendCompactCheckpoint`). v1 of this card wrongly claimed "no compaction for 5 weeks" — retracted: the owner watched compactions happen live; only the RECORD KIND differs.
- **The resume did not reproduce the pre-close fold projection.** Before close the visible context was ≈100k tokens (the fold markers in the transcript cover e.g. `0-439:ckpt·98k→3.4ktok`). After reopen the ctx meter showed **143% of 200k (≈286k) at idle boot, before any user message** — roughly the pre-close visible set PLUS a large fraction of folded debt back in view. The fold chain half-applied.

Primary suspects (need one repro to separate):
1. **RecordId anchor skew:** folds persist `recordIds`; a resume that rebuilds record identities differently across the CLI version boundary (or across branch/merge points) orphans the ranges → dropped.
2. **Depth-cap flattening divergence:** `engine.dart:767 _flattenForDepthCap` flattens nested `CompactCheckpointRecord`s — if boot's flatten pass differs from the live one (order/depth bookkeeping), the visible set grows.
3. **Version skew 1.0.531→1.0.532:** a record shape or ledger rule change between the binary that wrote the folds and the binary that replays them, silently skipping older folds.

Secondary legs (still true, now clearly subordinate):
- **S1 — no boot cap:** nothing force-compacts an over-window session at resume; the `force` path exists (`auto_compactor.dart:223/275`) but boot never uses it. The meter faithfully displayed 143% and waited.
- **S2 — gate blindness (consequence, not cause):** `auto_compactor.dart:263 _requestTokens()` gates on the post-fold visible list only. That is by design for structured compaction (folds are cheap, expansion on demand), but it is why the file grew to 2.01 GB of recoverable debt with no classic compaction record — the debt is invisible to every budget surface until a fold-loss event detonates it.
- **S3 — userTurn detonation:** a real user turn auto-closes checkpoints (`checkpoint_tool.dart:235 _stalenessReason`, #286 — correct) restoring hidden spans at once; without a budget guard this is a second path to the same balloon.

## Why this framing
Retracted (v1): "resume miscounts tokens" — the meter is honest. Retracted (v1→v2): "no compaction ran for 16k records" — structured compaction ran constantly; only classic records stopped. Kept: the detonation framing — several independent events (fold-loss resume, userTurn auto-close) can each push the live context far past the window, and nothing reconciles folded debt against any budget.

## Architecture
- **Fold-projection equivalence (primary fix):** the ledger replay at resume MUST reproduce the live engine's visible set — same fold application, same depth-cap flatten, same recordId resolution; verified by an equivalence property test (replay-vs-live byte-comparison of the projected payload on forked fixtures), not by spot checks.
- **Version-skew tolerance:** fold records carry enough shape metadata that a newer binary replays older folds or FAILS LOUD (a resume note naming the dropped fold generation), never silently half-applies.
- **Boot cap:** resume of an over-window session runs one forced compaction pass before the first request (S1); the meter renders the post-cap number.
- **Budget-guarded restore (S3):** checkpoint auto-close restores hidden spans only up to a budget; the remainder routes into a forced pass. Degradation: compactor failure → local trim (existing), never a silent over-window request.
- **ComposedBudgetEstimator (S2, second tier):** one pure function (visible + hidden debt) for the gate/meter/boot so debt is visible before it detonates.

## Capability surface (subject of every verb)
| capability | acts on | shape |
|---|---|---|
| replay | the **persisted fold chain** (`hidden_range`+`compact_checkpoint` records) | equivalence with the live projection, byte-verified |
| tolerate | **older fold record shapes** across CLI versions | loud-fail note listing dropped generations |
| cap | the **resumed context** at boot | one forced pass; meter shows post-cap |
| restore | **hidden spans** at checkpoint auto-close | budget-capped, remainder compacted |
| surface | the **composed budget** (visible+debt) | same number in gate/meter/boot (second tier) |

Tiering: **core** = fold-projection equivalence + loud version-skew failure + boot cap + budget-guarded restore. **Second tier** = ComposedBudgetEstimator surfaces, proactive debt compaction. **Excluded** = changing #286 auto-close semantics (correct design, wrong blast radius — fixed by the guard); JSONL GC/vacuum (own card; #503 owns parse cost); new TUI chrome.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** — replay equivalence: for a fixture session with nested folds, the resumed projection is byte-identical to the pre-close live projection (property test over fork points).
- **AC2** — version-skew loud-fail: a fold record the replaying binary cannot resolve produces a visible resume note naming the dropped generation; partial silent application is impossible (assert: applied-set ⊆ resolvable-set, all-or-note).
- **AC3** — boot cap: resume of an over-window session (fixture: pre-cap 143%) runs one forced pass; meter ≤ 100% at idle boot, before any user message.
- **AC4** — budget-guarded restore: a user turn that auto-closes checkpoints never leaves the live context above window−16,384; the remainder is compacted before the next request.
- **AC5** — compactor failure during AC3/AC4 degrades to local trim; the next request is still ≤ window; a failure note is recorded.

## Test plan
### Test matrix — maximal coverage, zero cross-platform breakage
- `UT-1` fold-chain replay purity (AC1): ledger folds applied by recordId; nested-depth flatten order; fork/merge points; byte-equality property vs live-engine projection on the same fixture.
- `UT-2` version-skew resolver (AC2): synthetic older-shape fold records → loud note, zero silent drops; resolvable-subset application is all-or-note.
- `UT-3` budget-guard arithmetic (AC4): restore order (newest-first), cap math, remainder routing.
- `IT-1` fake-clock marathon replay (AC1/AC4): scripted 16k-record ledger with 24 folds; close/resume cycle; user-turn injection mid-detour; context ≤ window−16,384 at every boundary.
- `IT-2` fake-provider resume boot (AC3/AC5): over-window fixture boots → forced pass → meter ≤ 100%; summarizer-failure fixture → local-trim fallback + note; kill/resume mid-pass (idempotent re-entry).
- `E2E-1` real CLI, the owner's exact repro: fold a marathon fixture under build A, close, resume under build B (A≠B); meter matches pre-close ±ε, or the loud note names the generation.
- `REG-1` fold-free sessions (the 99% case): byte-identical outbound payloads vs pre-change golden corpus.
- `REG-2` checkpoint UX (#286): detour auto-close notes, `checkpoint_auto_closed` audit records, rewind semantics untouched.

**vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit** (2026-10-08):
Scope check vs the normative issue #1425 body — delivered vs claimed: AC1 (replay equivalence) ✅, AC2 (version-skew loud-fail) ✅, AC3 (boot cap) ✅, AC5 (degrade) ✅, but **AC4 (budget-guarded restore at checkpoint auto-close) is absent** — no restore-budget leg, no user-turn injection test, no window−16384 guard. AC4 is CORE tier per the issue body ('core = equivalence + loud-fail + boot cap + budget-guarded restore'), and ComposedBudgetEstimator ('one number, three callers') is missing too (second-tier, defensibly deferred). 'Closes #1425' on a partial core-tier delivery auto-closes the card with its central detonation-guard (user-turn auto-close restoring all hidden spans at once) undelivered — that's the exact RCA path from the issue. Ask: either add the AC4 leg to this PR, or re-scope the linkage to 'Partially addresses #1425' + a follow-up card covering AC4 (+ the estimator), so the detonation path keeps an owner.

---

### Thread 9

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The three delivered legs are solid — kept-path residency at the classic boundary (AC1), all-or-note fold resolution (AC2), and the idle-boot cap with its degrade path (AC3/AC5) all analyze clean, pass their new tests (49 storage + 2 CLI + 345 compaction/auto-compactor green locally), and preserve REG-1 byte-shape rendering. The blocker is scope: **AC4 (budget-guarded restore at checkpoint auto-close) is still absent while the PR says "Closes #1425"** — the round-1 thread asked for the leg or a re-scope, and neither happened, so merging auto-closes the issue with its core detonation guard unowned.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1427
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1427
- **Title**: gh-1425 [GOAL] Resume loses structured-compaction folds — marathon session reopens at 143% of window make fold projection resume-equivalent and cap every detonation path
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1425` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 13
- **Additions**: +1612
- **Deletions**: -45
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T20:46:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T22:44:12Z

## PR Description

Closes #1425
# gh-1425 — Resume loses structured-compaction folds (marathon session)

### Root Cause
Resuming a marathon session did not reproduce the live fold projection — three legs:
- `WindowedSessionStorage.growOlderUntil` stopped the resume boundary walk when the branch *contained* the newest classic compaction record, but the kept region starts at `firstKeptEntryId` — a walk block-bottom landing inside the kept span silently dropped the whole kept region (residency skew), so folds half-applied over a different record population.
- `renderStructuredMessages` applied every fold record as-is, with no resolution check: a fold the replaying binary cannot resolve (an older writer stored the ids under keys this build does not read — empty id shape) still rendered its checkpoint text as a valid summary over nothing.
- Resume boot never capped an over-window session (the meter sat at 143% and waited); and the degraded local-trim valve kept `keepRecentTokens` *transcript* tokens while the trigger measures *request* tokens (incl. system-prompt/tool overhead), so a degraded boot landed back over the trigger and re-fired compaction on turn 1.

### Fix
- `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`: `growOlderUntil` now keeps paging until the classic boundary's `firstKeptEntryId` is resident (`ensureCompactionBoundaryResident`) — the resumed replay sees the full kept path.
- `lib/src/compaction/structured/projection.dart`: all-or-note fold resolution — a fold the replaying binary cannot resolve (empty id shape: an older writer's keys this build does not read) is dropped WHOLE, never applied, and a visible resume note names it (seq + kind). Off-path references (off-branch checkpoint coverage, below-window ranges) are not skew and render exactly as before (REG-1).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart` + `session_commands.dart`: resume boot cap — `_loadSession` runs one gated forced compaction pass at idle boot (also on mid-REPL session switches) so the meter renders the post-cap number before the first user message.
- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: `_localTrimFallback` clamps its kept budget to `min(keepRecentTokens, trigger − overhead)` so a degraded (summarizer-down) boot stays under the compaction trigger and the session remains usable without a working summarizer.

### Test Coverage
- `test/session/windowed_session_storage_test.dart` — boundary walk keeps paging until `firstKeptEntryId` is resident (RED before fix).
- `test/compaction/structured_resume_equivalence_test.dart` — live-vs-resume projection byte-shape equality over a marathon fixture with a forked branch and folded checkpoints; AC2 tests: empty-shape hidden range and checkpoint dropped whole with a note, off-path refs apply unchanged with no note.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_resume_boot_cap_test.dart` — AC3: cap pass runs before any user input and the next request fits the window; AC5: dead summarizer degrades to the visible `[context trimmed]` note, boot survives, turn 1 answers without re-firing compaction.
- Full suite: `dart test test/compaction test/agent test/cli` green (see notes on the earlier native abort).

### Notes
- Healthy fold rendering is intentionally unchanged (REG-1 asserted byte-shape equality) — only unresolvable folds change behavior, and only by becoming visible notes instead of silent half-applies.
- The resume note is one user-role message; it adds no hidden context and keeps the `window − reserve` invariant via the existing pre-flight gate.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files

# gh-1425: [GOAL] Resume loses structured-compaction folds — marathon session reopens at 143% of window; make fold projection resume-equivalent and cap every detonation path

## Description

## Goal — Compaction/checkpoint composition (v2)
One sentence: **a marathon session resumed after close/reopen restores the same visible context it had before the close — structured-compaction folds survive the resume byte-faithfully, and no single event (boot or user turn) can leave the live context above the model's window.**

Live RCA from a real 36-day session (`01a06644-7b1b-72b2-b9ea-2e1971a36251`, CLI updated 1.0.531→1.0.532 between close and reopen, 2026-10-08):

## RCA (measured on the session file, mechanisms pinned to code)
- Session JSONL: **2.01 GB, 19,112 records.** Kinds: 9,862 message, 9,131 custom, **6 classic `compaction` (last at index 3,081)**, 5 `branch_summary`, **24 `hidden_range`** (last at 19,040; 77 records / 1.74 MB after), **14 `compact_checkpoint`** (9,185→19,037).
- **Compaction DID run the whole time — as STRUCTURED compaction.** The classic LLM-summary `compaction` record stopped at 3,081; from there the structured engine owned the context: `hidden_range` + `compact_checkpoint` records ARE its folds (`engine.dart:260/413/540 appendHiddenRange(recordIds:…)`, `engine.dart:603 appendCompactCheckpoint`). v1 of this card wrongly claimed "no compaction for 5 weeks" — retracted: the owner watched compactions happen live; only the RECORD KIND differs.
- **The resume did not reproduce the pre-close fold projection.** Before close the visible context was ≈100k tokens (the fold markers in the transcript cover e.g. `0-439:ckpt·98k→3.4ktok`). After reopen the ctx meter showed **143% of 200k (≈286k) at idle boot, before any user message** — roughly the pre-close visible set PLUS a large fraction of folded debt back in view. The fold chain half-applied.

Primary suspects (need one repro to separate):
1. **RecordId anchor skew:** folds persist `recordIds`; a resume that rebuilds record identities differently across the CLI version boundary (or across branch/merge points) orphans the ranges → dropped.
2. **Depth-cap flattening divergence:** `engine.dart:767 _flattenForDepthCap` flattens nested `CompactCheckpointRecord`s — if boot's flatten pass differs from the live one (order/depth bookkeeping), the visible set grows.
3. **Version skew 1.0.531→1.0.532:** a record shape or ledger rule change between the binary that wrote the folds and the binary that replays them, silently skipping older folds.

Secondary legs (still true, now clearly subordinate):
- **S1 — no boot cap:** nothing force-compacts an over-window session at resume; the `force` path exists (`auto_compactor.dart:223/275`) but boot never uses it. The meter faithfully displayed 143% and waited.
- **S2 — gate blindness (consequence, not cause):** `auto_compactor.dart:263 _requestTokens()` gates on the post-fold visible list only. That is by design for structured compaction (folds are cheap, expansion on demand), but it is why the file grew to 2.01 GB of recoverable debt with no classic compaction record — the debt is invisible to every budget surface until a fold-loss event detonates it.
- **S3 — userTurn detonation:** a real user turn auto-closes checkpoints (`checkpoint_tool.dart:235 _stalenessReason`, #286 — correct) restoring hidden spans at once; without a budget guard this is a second path to the same balloon.

## Why this framing
Retracted (v1): "resume miscounts tokens" — the meter is honest. Retracted (v1→v2): "no compaction ran for 16k records" — structured compaction ran constantly; only classic records stopped. Kept: the detonation framing — several independent events (fold-loss resume, userTurn auto-close) can each push the live context far past the window, and nothing reconciles folded debt against any budget.

## Architecture
- **Fold-projection equivalence (primary fix):** the ledger replay at resume MUST reproduce the live engine's visible set — same fold application, same depth-cap flatten, same recordId resolution; verified by an equivalence property test (replay-vs-live byte-comparison of the projected payload on forked fixtures), not by spot checks.
- **Version-skew tolerance:** fold records carry enough shape metadata that a newer binary replays older folds or FAILS LOUD (a resume note naming the dropped fold generation), never silently half-applies.
- **Boot cap:** resume of an over-window session runs one forced compaction pass before the first request (S1); the meter renders the post-cap number.
- **Budget-guarded restore (S3):** checkpoint auto-close restores hidden spans only up to a budget; the remainder routes into a forced pass. Degradation: compactor failure → local trim (existing), never a silent over-window request.
- **ComposedBudgetEstimator (S2, second tier):** one pure function (visible + hidden debt) for the gate/meter/boot so debt is visible before it detonates.

## Capability surface (subject of every verb)
| capability | acts on | shape |
|---|---|---|
| replay | the **persisted fold chain** (`hidden_range`+`compact_checkpoint` records) | equivalence with the live projection, byte-verified |
| tolerate | **older fold record shapes** across CLI versions | loud-fail note listing dropped generations |
| cap | the **resumed context** at boot | one forced pass; meter shows post-cap |
| restore | **hidden spans** at checkpoint auto-close | budget-capped, remainder compacted |
| surface | the **composed budget** (visible+debt) | same number in gate/meter/boot (second tier) |

Tiering: **core** = fold-projection equivalence + loud version-skew failure + boot cap + budget-guarded restore. **Second tier** = ComposedBudgetEstimator surfaces, proactive debt compaction. **Excluded** = changing #286 auto-close semantics (correct design, wrong blast radius — fixed by the guard); JSONL GC/vacuum (own card; #503 owns parse cost); new TUI chrome.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** — replay equivalence: for a fixture session with nested folds, the resumed projection is byte-identical to the pre-close live projection (property test over fork points).
- **AC2** — version-skew loud-fail: a fold record the replaying binary cannot resolve produces a visible resume note naming the dropped generation; partial silent application is impossible (assert: applied-set ⊆ resolvable-set, all-or-note).
- **AC3** — boot cap: resume of an over-window session (fixture: pre-cap 143%) runs one forced pass; meter ≤ 100% at idle boot, before any user message.
- **AC4** — budget-guarded restore: a user turn that auto-closes checkpoints never leaves the live context above window−16,384; the remainder is compacted before the next request.
- **AC5** — compactor failure during AC3/AC4 degrades to local trim; the next request is still ≤ window; a failure note is recorded.

## Test plan
### Test matrix — maximal coverage, zero cross-platform breakage
- `UT-1` fold-chain replay purity (AC1): ledger folds applied by recordId; nested-depth flatten order; fork/merge points; byte-equality property vs live-engine projection on the same fixture.
- `UT-2` version-skew resolver (AC2): synthetic older-shape fold records → loud note, zero silent drops; resolvable-subset application is all-or-note.
- `UT-3` budget-guard arithmetic (AC4): restore order (newest-first), cap math, remainder routing.
- `IT-1` fake-clock marathon replay (AC1/AC4): scripted 16k-record ledger with 24 folds; close/resume cycle; user-turn injection mid-detour; context ≤ window−16,384 at every boundary.
- `IT-2` fake-provider resume boot (AC3/AC5): over-window fixture boots → forced pass → meter ≤ 100%; summarizer-failure fixture → local-trim fallback + note; kill/resume mid-pass (idempotent re-entry).
- `E2E-1` real CLI, the owner's exact repro: fold a marathon fixture under build A, close, resume under build B (A≠B); meter matches pre-close ±ε, or the loud note names the generation.
- `REG-1` fold-free sessions (the 99% case): byte-identical outbound payloads vs pre-change golden corpus.
- `REG-2` checkpoint UX (#286): detour auto-close notes, `checkpoint_auto_closed` audit records, rewind semantics untouched.

So the interplay with the new `_keptPathResident` requirement:
- Boundary found but kept path not resident → walk continues (instead of returning true).
- If the budget stop fires first → `_trimTokenBudget` + return **true** → the CLI boots windowed WITHOUT the boundary/kept path — the classic transform then sees NO compaction record → renders the whole resident tail. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1427
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1427
- **Title**: gh-1425 [GOAL] Resume loses structured-compaction folds — marathon session reopens at 143% of window make fold projection resume-equivalent and cap every detonation path
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1425` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 13
- **Additions**: +1612
- **Deletions**: -45
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T20:46:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T22:44:12Z

## PR Description

Closes #1425
# gh-1425 — Resume loses structured-compaction folds (marathon session)

### Root Cause
Resuming a marathon session did not reproduce the live fold projection — three legs:
- `WindowedSessionStorage.growOlderUntil` stopped the resume boundary walk when the branch *contained* the newest classic compaction record, but the kept region starts at `firstKeptEntryId` — a walk block-bottom landing inside the kept span silently dropped the whole kept region (residency skew), so folds half-applied over a different record population.
- `renderStructuredMessages` applied every fold record as-is, with no resolution check: a fold the replaying binary cannot resolve (an older writer stored the ids under keys this build does not read — empty id shape) still rendered its checkpoint text as a valid summary over nothing.
- Resume boot never capped an over-window session (the meter sat at 143% and waited); and the degraded local-trim valve kept `keepRecentTokens` *transcript* tokens while the trigger measures *request* tokens (incl. system-prompt/tool overhead), so a degraded boot landed back over the trigger and re-fired compaction on turn 1.

### Fix
- `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`: `growOlderUntil` now keeps paging until the classic boundary's `firstKeptEntryId` is resident (`ensureCompactionBoundaryResident`) — the resumed replay sees the full kept path.
- `lib/src/compaction/structured/projection.dart`: all-or-note fold resolution — a fold the replaying binary cannot resolve (empty id shape: an older writer's keys this build does not read) is dropped WHOLE, never applied, and a visible resume note names it (seq + kind). Off-path references (off-branch checkpoint coverage, below-window ranges) are not skew and render exactly as before (REG-1).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart` + `session_commands.dart`: resume boot cap — `_loadSession` runs one gated forced compaction pass at idle boot (also on mid-REPL session switches) so the meter renders the post-cap number before the first user message.
- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: `_localTrimFallback` clamps its kept budget to `min(keepRecentTokens, trigger − overhead)` so a degraded (summarizer-down) boot stays under the compaction trigger and the session remains usable without a working summarizer.

### Test Coverage
- `test/session/windowed_session_storage_test.dart` — boundary walk keeps paging until `firstKeptEntryId` is resident (RED before fix).
- `test/compaction/structured_resume_equivalence_test.dart` — live-vs-resume projection byte-shape equality over a marathon fixture with a forked branch and folded checkpoints; AC2 tests: empty-shape hidden range and checkpoint dropped whole with a note, off-path refs apply unchanged with no note.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_resume_boot_cap_test.dart` — AC3: cap pass runs before any user input and the next request fits the window; AC5: dead summarizer degrades to the visible `[context trimmed]` note, boot survives, turn 1 answers without re-firing compaction.
- Full suite: `dart test test/compaction test/agent test/cli` green (see notes on the earlier native abort).

### Notes
- Healthy fold rendering is intentionally unchanged (REG-1 asserted byte-shape equality) — only unresolvable folds change behavior, and only by becoming visible notes instead of silent half-applies.
- The resume note is one user-role message; it adds no hidden context and keeps the `window − reserve` invariant via the existing pre-flight gate.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.

# gh-1425: [GOAL] Resume loses structured-compaction folds — marathon session reopens at 143% of window; make fold projection resume-equivalent and cap every detonation path

## Description

## Goal — Compaction/checkpoint composition (v2)
One sentence: **a marathon session resumed after close/reopen restores the same visible context it had before the close — structured-compaction folds survive the resume byte-faithfully, and no single event (boot or user turn) can leave the live context above the model's window.**

Live RCA from a real 36-day session (`01a06644-7b1b-72b2-b9ea-2e1971a36251`, CLI updated 1.0.531→1.0.532 between close and reopen, 2026-10-08):

## RCA (measured on the session file, mechanisms pinned to code)
- Session JSONL: **2.01 GB, 19,112 records.** Kinds: 9,862 message, 9,131 custom, **6 classic `compaction` (last at index 3,081)**, 5 `branch_summary`, **24 `hidden_range`** (last at 19,040; 77 records / 1.74 MB after), **14 `compact_checkpoint`** (9,185→19,037).
- **Compaction DID run the whole time — as STRUCTURED compaction.** The classic LLM-summary `compaction` record stopped at 3,081; from there the structured engine owned the context: `hidden_range` + `compact_checkpoint` records ARE its folds (`engine.dart:260/413/540 appendHiddenRange(recordIds:…)`, `engine.dart:603 appendCompactCheckpoint`). v1 of this card wrongly claimed "no compaction for 5 weeks" — retracted: the owner watched compactions happen live; only the RECORD KIND differs.
- **The resume did not reproduce the pre-close fold projection.** Before close the visible context was ≈100k tokens (the fold markers in the transcript cover e.g. `0-439:ckpt·98k→3.4ktok`). After reopen the ctx meter showed **143% of 200k (≈286k) at idle boot, before any user message** — roughly the pre-close visible set PLUS a large fraction of folded debt back in view. The fold chain half-applied.

Primary suspects (need one repro to separate):
1. **RecordId anchor skew:** folds persist `recordIds`; a resume that rebuilds record identities differently across the CLI version boundary (or across branch/merge points) orphans the ranges → dropped.
2. **Depth-cap flattening divergence:** `engine.dart:767 _flattenForDepthCap` flattens nested `CompactCheckpointRecord`s — if boot's flatten pass differs from the live one (order/depth bookkeeping), the visible set grows.
3. **Version skew 1.0.531→1.0.532:** a record shape or ledger rule change between the binary that wrote the folds and the binary that replays them, silently skipping older folds.

Secondary legs (still true, now clearly subordinate):
- **S1 — no boot cap:** nothing force-compacts an over-window session at resume; the `force` path exists (`auto_compactor.dart:223/275`) but boot never uses it. The meter faithfully displayed 143% and waited.
- **S2 — gate blindness (consequence, not cause):** `auto_compactor.dart:263 _requestTokens()` gates on the post-fold visible list only. That is by design for structured compaction (folds are cheap, expansion on demand), but it is why the file grew to 2.01 GB of recoverable debt with no classic compaction record — the debt is invisible to every budget surface until a fold-loss event detonates it.
- **S3 — userTurn detonation:** a real user turn auto-closes checkpoints (`checkpoint_tool.dart:235 _stalenessReason`, #286 — correct) restoring hidden spans at once; without a budget guard this is a second path to the same balloon.

## Why this framing
Retracted (v1): "resume miscounts tokens" — the meter is honest. Retracted (v1→v2): "no compaction ran for 16k records" — structured compaction ran constantly; only classic records stopped. Kept: the detonation framing — several independent events (fold-loss resume, userTurn auto-close) can each push the live context far past the window, and nothing reconciles folded debt against any budget.

## Architecture
- **Fold-projection equivalence (primary fix):** the ledger replay at resume MUST reproduce the live engine's visible set — same fold application, same depth-cap flatten, same recordId resolution; verified by an equivalence property test (replay-vs-live byte-comparison of the projected payload on forked fixtures), not by spot checks.
- **Version-skew tolerance:** fold records carry enough shape metadata that a newer binary replays older folds or FAILS LOUD (a resume note naming the dropped fold generation), never silently half-applies.
- **Boot cap:** resume of an over-window session runs one forced compaction pass before the first request (S1); the meter renders the post-cap number.
- **Budget-guarded restore (S3):** checkpoint auto-close restores hidden spans only up to a budget; the remainder routes into a forced pass. Degradation: compactor failure → local trim (existing), never a silent over-window request.
- **ComposedBudgetEstimator (S2, second tier):** one pure function (visible + hidden debt) for the gate/meter/boot so debt is visible before it detonates.

## Capability surface (subject of every verb)
| capability | acts on | shape |
|---|---|---|
| replay | the **persisted fold chain** (`hidden_range`+`compact_checkpoint` records) | equivalence with the live projection, byte-verified |
| tolerate | **older fold record shapes** across CLI versions | loud-fail note listing dropped generations |
| cap | the **resumed context** at boot | one forced pass; meter shows post-cap |
| restore | **hidden spans** at checkpoint auto-close | budget-capped, remainder compacted |
| surface | the **composed budget** (visible+debt) | same number in gate/meter/boot (second tier) |

Tiering: **core** = fold-projection equivalence + loud version-skew failure + boot cap + budget-guarded restore. **Second tier** = ComposedBudgetEstimator surfaces, proactive debt compaction. **Excluded** = changing #286 auto-close semantics (correct design, wrong blast radius — fixed by the guard); JSONL GC/vacuum (own card; #503 owns parse cost); new TUI chrome.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** — replay equivalence: for a fixture session with nested folds, the resumed projection is byte-identical to the pre-close live projection (property test over fork points).
- **AC2** — version-skew loud-fail: a fold record the replaying binary cannot resolve produces a visible resume note naming the dropped generation; partial silent application is impossible (assert: applied-set ⊆ resolvable-set, all-or-note).
- **AC3** — boot cap: resume of an over-window session (fixture: pre-cap 143%) runs one forced pass; meter ≤ 100% at idle boot, before any user message.
- **AC4** — budget-guarded restore: a user turn that auto-closes checkpoints never leaves the live context above window−16,384; the remainder is compacted before the next request.
- **AC5** — compactor failure during AC3/AC4 degrades to local trim; the next request is still ≤ window; a failure note is recorded.

## Test plan
### Test matrix — maximal coverage, zero cross-platform breakage
- `UT-1` fold-chain replay purity (AC1): ledger folds applied by recordId; nested-depth flatten order; fork/merge points; byte-equality property vs live-engine projection on the same fixture.
- `UT-2` version-skew resolver (AC2): synthetic older-shape fold records → loud note, zero silent drops; resolvable-subset application is all-or-note.
- `UT-3` budget-guard arithmetic (AC4): restore order (newest-first), cap math, remainder routing.
- `IT-1` fake-clock marathon replay (AC1/AC4): scripted 16k-record ledger with 24 folds; close/resume cycle; user-turn injection mid-detour; context ≤ window−16,384 at every boundary.
- `IT-2` fake-provider resume boot (AC3/AC5): over-window fixture boots → forced pass → meter ≤ 100%; summarizer-failure fixture → local-trim fallback + note; kill/resume mid-pass (idempotent re-entry).
- `E2E-1` real CLI, the owner's exact repro: fold a marathon fixture under build A, close, resume under build B (A≠B); meter matches pre-close ±ε, or the loud note names the generation.
- `REG-1` fold-free sessions (the 99% case): byte-identical outbound payloads vs pre-change golden corpus.
- `REG-2` checkpoint UX (#286): detour auto-close notes, `checkpoint_auto_closed` audit records, rewind semantics untouched.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1427
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1427
- **Title**: gh-1425 [GOAL] Resume loses structured-compaction folds — marathon session reopens at 143% of window make fold projection resume-equivalent and cap every detonation path
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1425` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 13
- **Additions**: +1612
- **Deletions**: -45
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T20:46:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T22:44:12Z

## PR Description

Closes #1425
# gh-1425 — Resume loses structured-compaction folds (marathon session)

### Root Cause
Resuming a marathon session did not reproduce the live fold projection — three legs:
- `WindowedSessionStorage.growOlderUntil` stopped the resume boundary walk when the branch *contained* the newest classic compaction record, but the kept region starts at `firstKeptEntryId` — a walk block-bottom landing inside the kept span silently dropped the whole kept region (residency skew), so folds half-applied over a different record population.
- `renderStructuredMessages` applied every fold record as-is, with no resolution check: a fold the replaying binary cannot resolve (an older writer stored the ids under keys this build does not read — empty id shape) still rendered its checkpoint text as a valid summary over nothing.
- Resume boot never capped an over-window session (the meter sat at 143% and waited); and the degraded local-trim valve kept `keepRecentTokens` *transcript* tokens while the trigger measures *request* tokens (incl. system-prompt/tool overhead), so a degraded boot landed back over the trigger and re-fired compaction on turn 1.

### Fix
- `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`: `growOlderUntil` now keeps paging until the classic boundary's `firstKeptEntryId` is resident (`ensureCompactionBoundaryResident`) — the resumed replay sees the full kept path.
- `lib/src/compaction/structured/projection.dart`: all-or-note fold resolution — a fold the replaying binary cannot resolve (empty id shape: an older writer's keys this build does not read) is dropped WHOLE, never applied, and a visible resume note names it (seq + kind). Off-path references (off-branch checkpoint coverage, below-window ranges) are not skew and render exactly as before (REG-1).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart` + `session_commands.dart`: resume boot cap — `_loadSession` runs one gated forced compaction pass at idle boot (also on mid-REPL session switches) so the meter renders the post-cap number before the first user message.
- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: `_localTrimFallback` clamps its kept budget to `min(keepRecentTokens, trigger − overhead)` so a degraded (summarizer-down) boot stays under the compaction trigger and the session remains usable without a working summarizer.

### Test Coverage
- `test/session/windowed_session_storage_test.dart` — boundary walk keeps paging until `firstKeptEntryId` is resident (RED before fix).
- `test/compaction/structured_resume_equivalence_test.dart` — live-vs-resume projection byte-shape equality over a marathon fixture with a forked branch and folded checkpoints; AC2 tests: empty-shape hidden range and checkpoint dropped whole with a note, off-path refs apply unchanged with no note.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_resume_boot_cap_test.dart` — AC3: cap pass runs before any user input and the next request fits the window; AC5: dead summarizer degrades to the visible `[context trimmed]` note, boot survives, turn 1 answers without re-firing compaction.
- Full suite: `dart test test/compaction test/agent test/cli` green (see notes on the earlier native abort).

### Notes
- Healthy fold rendering is intentionally unchanged (REG-1 asserted byte-shape equality) — only unresolvable folds change behavior, and only by becoming visible notes instead of silent half-applies.
- The resume note is one user-role message; it adds no hidden context and keeps the `window − reserve` invariant via the existing pre-flight gate.
